statements.proposition: The rewritten scripts/terraform/deploy.py entry point in this change keeps backward compatibility with the existing deployment workflow (the same invocation still works as before).
statements.label: FALSE
statements.note: Impact claim settled by a concrete interface check: the base README's documented workflow is 'terraform plan/apply' then 'python deploy.py', which non-interactively read Terraform outputs (key_data_1/2, public_ip_address_1/2) and ran kubeadm/controller/setup scripts over SSH. At head, 'python deploy.py' instead prompts on stdin for resource group, prefix, region and confirmation and runs deploy_unified.py deploy (full provisioning). The old logic was moved to a new file deploy_legacy.py, so the old workflow survives only under a different name. Terraform side stays compatible by default (create_resource_group defaults to false), but the statement is about the deploy.py entry point. Judgment flagged because 'existing workflows' is vague; if read as 'Ansible playbooks still usable' it could be TRUE.
